meanings: noun: a set of beliefs or a culture that is passed from family to family over a long period of time
examples: Chris's favorite tradition is eating ham on Christmas.

meanings: adjective: large enough or important enough to get special notice
examples: A considerable number of popular sports were invented in only the last 100 years.

meanings: noun: possible ability that might be used in the future
adjective: having the ability to do something in the future
examples: Wind and solar energy have the potential to replace oil.
China is potentially the next world leader.

meanings: verb: to be a different size, amount, or character when compared to something else in a similar group
examples: The restaurants in this area vary greatly in quality and price.

meanings: verb: to give something (often money); to help reach a goal
verb: to add to the cause of something bigger
examples: Over the past three years, my parents have not contributed to my university tuition.
I smoked a lot when I was younger, and that has contributed to my health problems today.

meanings: adjective: not likely to change, fall, or move; secure (in employment, finances, housing, etc)
examples: Make sure the ladder is stable before you climb up it!

meanings: noun: a group of people living or working together
examples: The Spanish-speaking community within New York City includes millions of people.

meanings: verb: to spend money, energy, or time on something hoping for good results later
verb: to spend money in the hopes of making more money, usually in property, financial shares, or some other activity
examples: If you want to learn another language, you will have to invest a lot of your free time.
Jamie invested in an education company that he thought would succeed and make him rich.

meanings: noun: a job or function; a position
examples: The student class president has an important role.

meanings: verb: to attach something so that it won't come off
verb: to get something important (especially when difficult)
adjective: to be safe; to be well attached
examples: Please tightly secure the surfboards on top of the car.
Animals in cold areas often work hard to secure food for the winter.
Your money will be more secure in a bank.

meanings: noun: one of several things that covers something else
verb: to cover something with several coverings
examples: Layers of paint on the steel bridge will protect it from salt water.
Sebastian layered the sandwich with all my favorite meats and cheeses.

meanings: verb: to get or secure something
examples: After lots of looking, Jorge obtained a job and apartment in New York City.

meanings: verb: to make something possible
examples: The classes in college will enable you to find a good job.

meanings: verb: to move something a short distance
noun: a small change in position or direction
examples: Please help me shift the table so it is easier for people to sit down.
The coach's recent shift in strategy is helping the team win more games.

meanings: verb: to begin or continue with some action
examples: We will not proceed with the construction until someone tells us it is safe to build here.

meanings: adjective: clearly different from another thing
examples: There are at least five distinct types of turtle living on the island.

meanings: noun: the distance between two things (like area, time, or intelligence)
verb: to be between a set minimum and maximum
examples: The range of scores on the test was large.
In the company, the age of the workers ranges from 25 to 75.

meanings: noun: the running of something or an organization (business, school, government, etc); the person or people in charge of running an organization
examples: The university administration cancelled all school events after a bad storm left most buildings without electricity.

meanings: verb: to give an event or person credit for something (like a work of art or a speech)
noun: a quality or feature that is an important part of something
examples: The museum director attributed the recently discovered painting to Van Gogh.
All of his movies have a few attributes in common: for example, there is little conversation and a lot of music.

meanings: verb: to argue, usually in a formal, polite way
noun: a formal, polite argument
examples: The importance of space travel is strongly debated.
Watching the presidential debates on TV did not help me decide who to vote for.

meanings: noun: a system of connected pieces (especially for transportation or communication)
examples: The typhoon destroyed the network of roads, which has made it hard to bring supplies and first aid to the town.

meanings: verb: to focus attention on something
verb: to come together into a smaller space
examples: You must learn to concentrate to be successful on the test.
The protests were concentrated in the city parks.

meanings: verb: to help something continue; to keep going
examples: No animals or plants can sustain life without water.

meanings: adjective: found or happening inside (a body, organization, or thing)
examples: The US government has had lots of problems ever since internal messages were published on news websites.

meanings: verb: to disagree with each other; to be impossible together
noun: an argument, long battle, or difference of opinions
examples: We want to eat delicious food, but that sometimes conflicts with our need to be healthy.
The conflict in Syria has forced many people to leave the country.

meanings: noun: something good coming from an action, agreement, idea, or plan
examples: The president flew around the country, talking about the benefits of the new health care law.

meanings: verb: to politely say no to an invitation or offer
verb: to become less, fewer, or smaller (usually of something good)
noun: a slow continuous loss of value, power, or strength
examples: I declined dinner because I had plans to eat with my family instead.
For ten years, the number of fish in the river has declined.
Many people say that America is in decline.

meanings: adjective: yearly; happening every year
examples: Everyone in Manchester was excited about the annual game between the city's two soccer teams.

meanings: verb: to figure out or explain the meaning of something
examples: The students could not interpret the extremely old book because the pages were hard to read.

meanings: adjective: exact; carefully defined
examples: Because the pirates weren't certain of the precise location of the gold, they dug holes all over the island.

meanings: verb: to show or reveal something that was hidden
examples: The politician's crimes were exposed and he was forced to leave his position.

meanings: noun: a belief; an idea
examples: I think the professor's notion of fun was different from the students' notion of fun.

meanings: noun: other possibility or option
adjective: different; other than the main option
examples: The menu includes alternatives for students who don't eat meat.
Many words in these flashcards have alternative definitions.

meanings: noun: a set way of thinking or a set feeling about something or someone
examples: Zach always has a positive attitude when he has to deal with a problem at work.

meanings: verb: to give out something
examples: The teacher distributed tests to the class, and the students were happy to see they did well.

meanings: noun: the location of something
examples: The people of the city voted for a site downtown as the location of the new sports stadium.

meanings: adjective: to have knowledge of
examples: As Helen drove away from the gas station, she wasn't aware that her lights were off until she turned onto a dark street.

meanings: verb: to have control over a process so that it functions properly
examples: Parents regulate the amount of time kids spend playing games on their phones.

meanings: adjective: happening or being before
examples: The new CEO of Yahoo called the prior CEO of the company to get a better understanding of the company.

meanings: noun: work; effort
examples: Juan was surprised at how much labor was needed to finish his project on time.

meanings: noun: the study of knowledge or a set of theories knowledge and thought
noun: a basic idea of a person or organization that affects their actions
examples: Philosophy has always tried to answer the question "What is the meaning of life?"
My philosophy is that if you can do something today, you shouldn't wait until tomorrow.

meanings: verb: to create a connection between two or more things
noun: a connection between two things
examples: The news story linked the president's success with the improved economy.
What is the link between success in life and in education?

meanings: verb: to be a close match
verb: to send letters back and forth
examples: This new paint for the room does not correspond to the old paint.
My mother and father corresponded for almost two years before meeting in person.

meanings: noun: a part of something (usually part of an idea)
examples: The element of his speech that I didn't like was at the end, when he talked about religion.

meanings: verb: to roughly determine the value or number of something; to guess a number using some information
examples: Be careful to not forget any costs for the year when you estimate your budget.

meanings: noun: the rank or social class of someone or something
noun: the current situation that something is in
examples: The status of women has slowly improved over the past 100 years, and it continues to improve.
What's the status of the new library? Are they finished building it yet?

meanings: adjective: equal
examples: A shoe size of 30 in Japan is equivalent to size 13 in the USA.

meanings: noun: control or responsibility (over people, area, or laws)
examples: Only Congress has the authority to make and pass laws for the country.

meanings: verb: to live (in a place)
examples: I reside in sunny California.

meanings: adjective: at the beginning
examples: My initial plan was to study until midnight and wake up late, but then I fell asleep early.
